fns.desc: tncs_deinit() frees each tncs->imv_data[i].imv_send but never NULLs the pointer afterward; if tncs_deinit were ever re-entered or the struct reused/inspected post-free, this is a stale/dangling pointer (defense-in-depth gap, not exploitable in current single-free-then-os_free(tncs) call pattern)

tncs_global_init(): if tncs_read_config() fails partway after having linked some struct tnc_if_imv nodes into tncs_global_data->imv, goto failed calls tncs_global_deinit() which correctly walks and frees imv list -- verified NOT a leak, no FN here

tncs_global_init(): if tncs_load_imv() fails for imv[k], goto failed -> tncs_global_deinit() frees the whole imv list via tncs_unload_imv (calls tncs_free_imv), so no leak; confirmed clean, not a real FN
tncs_process_if_tnccs(): dup_binstr()'d buf is freed on every early-return path (:793,:804,:818,:826) as well as the normal exit (:947) -- verified clean, no FN
